text:
maria.g: :warning: ap-southeast GPU nodepool reports 100% allocatable used, a bunch of inference pods are Pending. Seeing very long queue times for realtime endpoints.
ops-bot: [ALERT] gpu-pool-apac-high-usage - 100% capacity - triggered at 1805127885. Auto-scaler events suppressed due to taints.
ajay: which nodepool? can you paste `kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool`?
maria.g: it's gpu-rt-pool-apac. quick `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Pending` shows ~22 pending, most with reason=Unschedulable.
dave: any OOMs or preemptions? maybe spot churn.
maria.g: no OOMs, nodes are just full (GPU resources). autoscaler logs show backoff: `scaleUp: skipped: no capacity in region or scaling suppressed by taints`.
autoscaler-bot: [cluster-autoscaler] Scale-up failed: node group gpu-rt-pool-apac reached max size (8) at 1805127902. Suggest increase max-nodes or create new nodegroup.
lina: wait, max size 8? that's low for peak inference. who set that?
ajay: that was an emergency cap put in last quarter to control costs. we didn't bump for PLG spikes.
dave: quick mitigation: 1) cordon the biggest GPU node hosting long-running batch jobs, 2) evict runaway jobs from gpu-rt-pool-apac to free GPUs, 3) temporarily raise max node count to 20. can we do that now?
maria.g: trying to identify big jobs. `kubectl top pods -n batch | sort -k3 -nr | head` shows 3 jobs using 4 GPUs each. one job stuck in CrashLoop but still holds resources.
ajay: ok kill that CrashLoop job: `kubectl delete pod job-encoder-7x9 -n batch` — i'll do it.
ajay: done. freed 4 GPUs, pending queue reduced to 18 -> 14. latency still bad.
lina: finance ok if we spin extra capacity for 6 hrs? cc @finance?
maria.g: dropping a temp play: `gcloud container node-pools update CONTAINER_CLUSTER --node-pool gpu-rt-pool-apac --max-nodes 20` (planning to run now).
ops-bot: running ramp:api has created request to GCP to raise nodepool max to 20 at 1805127940.
autoscaler-bot: [cluster-autoscaler] Detected scaling event: requesting 6 nodes for gpu-rt-pool-apac. Will attempt allocation in next 45s.
aday: (typo) sorry - meant ajay.
ajay: new nodes are booting. meanwhile, suggestion: add autoscaler flag `--expendable-pods-priority-cutoff` to avoid blocking critical endpoints with low-priority batch.
dave: good call. Also consider setting `balance-similar-node-groups` to false? not sure.
lina: can we route non-critical load to cpu-fallback models until GPUs come up? would add ~200ms latency but keep availability.
maria.g: implemented quick traffic-split via nginx ingress weight change for endpoint inference-prod: `curl -X POST /admin/split -d '{"cpu":0.25, "gpu":0.75}'` — routing started 2m ago.
ajay: nodepool scaled to 14 by 1805128025. pending pods dropped to 6, p95 latency improving.
ops-bot: NOTE: observed a scaling storm risk - many small pods requesting GPUs causing frequent scale-up decisions. consider autoscaler stabilization windows.
dave: set `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 15m might help. also we need quota request to cloud for more GPUs per region. I'll file infra ticket.
lina: opened infra#4721 to request quota bump and new nodepool for apac dedicated inference.
ajay: action items for post-mortem: 1) increase max nodes for gpu-rt-pool-apac to 50 during peak hours, 2) add priority classes so batch doesn't block real-time, 3) autoscaler flags tuned, 4) set warm standby nodes or spare capacity, 5) implement cost alerting for burst spend.
maria.g: will start post-incident notes and add timeline. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident resolved: capacity increased, routing fallback engaged, tail latency returned to normal. Closing alert at 1805128188.
lina: leaving final note: remember to add canary traffic tests for cpu-fallback before next spike. :eyes:
